summary: Backend testing for iteration 45 - NEW Projects (Cronograma) module. All 18 pytest cases passed (100%). Validated: admin CRUD, supervisor 403 restrictions, progress-only PATCH clamp (-25→0, 250→100, 42.5 preserved), hierarchical parent/child tasks, cascade delete (parent + 2 subs removed together), auto-recalc end_date (with and without lock_end_date), PDF generation (landscape A4, %PDF header, >1KB, both query-token and Bearer header auth, 401 without token, download=1 attachment vs inline). OneDrive webhook skip log confirmed ('OneDrive webhook (project) not configured; skipping upload'). Regression: /api/reports and /api/timesheets remain 200. Cleanup ran successfully.
critical_code_review_comments: projects.py PDF endpoint total_days can be 1 when proj_start==proj_end; Gantt with a single-day column is fine but if any task end_date extends beyond proj_end (rare with recalc off/lock=True and manual dates), end_idx is clamped to total_days-1 which may compress bars visually — acceptable edge case.
add_task/update_task use replace_one for the whole document; on high concurrency this could overwrite other concurrent task updates. Consider $set with array filters if concurrency ever grows.
delete_project does not verify the project exists before returning ok:true (returns ok even for non-existent id). Consider 404 for better client feedback.

PATCH progress endpoint uses get_current_user without role check — any authenticated user (including future non-supervisor roles) could update progress. Current app has only Admin+Supervisor so effectively fine, but worth documenting.
PDF endpoint accepts token via query string which will be logged in access logs (see backend log). Consider adding a note or a token exchange for secure links.
